name: Milo Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Milo' was chosen for Luo Zheng's late father Luo Xiao, and he carries the family surname 'Lowell' to keep the protagonist's family unit consistent.
description: Zane Lowell's father and the former lord of House Lowell, deceased years before the story begins. Source chapters confirm he was murdered through a plot by rival kinsmen and the Qi Family's patriarch (localized as the rival county houses that 'took their cut from Milo's death'). His legendary sword and legacy drive Zane's return to Castermere County, where leadership of the house passes to Zane.

name: Body Refining
reason: The source cultivation path of 'Body Refiners' who temper the physical body was kept nearly verbatim as 'Body Refining' since the term already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A cultivation system separate from Vitality cultivation, in which the practitioner tempers the physical body directly. Per the master sheet it involves refining 108 Nexus Points using Law Power such as flame and lightning, mirroring the source's Body Refiners who temper acupoints with thunder and fire. Ogre martial artists are noted as being devoted to Body Refining.

name: Deathly Canticle
issues: MasterLS attributes Deathly Canticles to Johanson's Shadow Group assassination art (Eps 270+), but Eps 256-259 use the term for Richard's (source Zhou Dan's) brush-written 'Kill' word constructs of the Thirteen Kills array; possible reuse of one localized term for two related techniques.
reason: The source's animated 'Kill' characters that form Zhou Dan's Thirteen Kills Formation were renamed 'Deathly Canticles', trading the untranslatable Chinese word-magic imagery for a Western occult-chant register.
description: Lethal word-constructs that make up the Array of Thirteen Kills. Their creator, Richard, writes them with a brush and continually replenishes destroyed Canticles at a modest Vitality cost, matching the source scene where Zhou Dan's 'Kill' words are worn down faster than he can rewrite them. Zane's Shadow Phantoms intercept and shatter them during the duel in Eps 256-259.

name: White Bone Armor
reason: The source term 'White Bone Armor' (also rendered 'White Bone Battle Armor') was carried over verbatim, as the macabre imagery already suits the Western fantasy register.
description: A defensive technique that encases its user in bone-like armor summoned from a swirl of crimson mist, sealing every gap from head to toe and sprouting lethal horns. In the episodes it is the signature protection of Jacob (source Wang Yun), who fights like a human tank inside it during the All Peaks Competition arc (Eps 262-287).

name: Bastian
reason: The character's Chinese name Qin Gang was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Bastian Kane' gives the brash young competitor a distinctive two-part Western name.
description: A Misty Peak student holding the sixth-highest rank in his peak, with one of the worst records in the All Peaks Competition. In Ep 271 Tracy punishes his disrespect with a gray bolt that punches straight through his chest and out his back, matching the source scene where a green-grey light pierces Qin Gang's chest. His fate becomes a cautionary memory for the crowd when Zane later faces Tracy.

name: House Hawthorne
reason: The source's Huang Family of Chongyang County was localized as 'House Hawthorne', preserving the H- initial while fitting the adaptation's 'House' naming convention for noble families.
description: The most powerful family in Castermere County during Zane's homecoming arc (Eps 327-337), ruled by Lord Chuck with his son Darcy (source Huang Xing). Once beneath House Lowell's notice, it rose by absorbing the Lowells' wealth after Milo's death, forcing other families to bow and surrender the lion's share of the county's riches. Zane kills Darcy and cuts off Chuck's hands, forcing the house to compensate House Lowell.

name: Level Three
reason: Generic ordinal sub-level phrase ('Level Three of the Adept Realm'), not a standalone entity; the realm names themselves are the tracked entities.

name: Providence Sect
reason: The source's 'Lucky Cloud Sect' was renamed 'Providence Sect', replacing the literal 'lucky' with the loftier synonym 'providence' and dropping the repetitive '-Cloud' pattern shared by the trial sects.
description: One of the sects participating in the Cloud Road Trial (Eps 359-374), with its Leader present at the Scrying Slate. Its star pupil is Lewis Bailey, billed as a once-in-a-millennium talent and 'the most charming man in the Providence Sect', matching the source's Red Maple, heartthrob of the Lucky Cloud Sect. Lewis is badly underestimated by rival cultivators before the ace's fall from grace.

name: Sixth-Tier Sect
reason: The source classification 'Sixth Grade Sect' was localized as 'Sixth-Tier Sect', swapping 'grade' for the more natural English ranking word 'tier'.
description: A fallen sect of the sixth tier, the highest-ranked power associated with the Cloud Road trial; its hidden inheritance and treasures, unlocked by the Crystal Key, are what the trial sects' students are really chasing (Eps 391-397). In the source it was the Blood Demon Emperor's Sixth Grade Sect, whose surviving legacy dwarfs anything the Cloud Hall possesses. Its ruins are reachable by teleportation array as late as Ep 970.

name: Dominic
reason: The character's Chinese name Li Buyi was fully localized to 'Dominic', a strong US-origin name fitting a top disciple of the Elite House.
description: A top disciple of the Cloud Hall's Elite House at the peak of the Soul Realm, known for his Longfist style (Eps 414-453). Like the source's Li Buyi, he is puzzled that Zane lacks the distinctive aura body refiners give off, and he is among the first to sense that Zane is something special. He later tests Zane with a full-power Core Strength strike.

name: Earth Law
reason: The source term 'Law of Earth' was rendered as 'Earth Law', a compact variant consistent with the show's law-naming pattern.
description: One of the elemental Laws of the world, governing earth and stone. Practitioners shape it into massive constructs such as protective shells around weapons and a mountain-leveling giant with enormous hands (Eps 1146-1233), and it can be shattered by sufficiently overwhelming force.

name: Madame Vermillion
reason: The source character is known only by her title, the Dragon Abyss Palace Master; the adaptation gave her the evocative proper name 'Madame Vermillion' to suit her status and the Western fantasy register.
description: Head of the Dragonfall Palace (source Dragon Abyss Palace) and a supreme figure among the Dragon-blooded, separated from ordinary members by an ocean-wide gulf in status (Eps 447-550). Though her eyes hold millennia of secrets, the source describes her maintaining the appearance of a sixteen-year-old girl, her lifespan measured in tens of thousands of years. She protects Zane during his breakthrough to the Fighting Soul level and takes a playful, amused interest in him.

name: Luck-Devouring Snakes
reason: The source's 'Luck Destroying Yellow Snakes' were renamed 'Luck-Devouring Snakes', tightening the phrase and dropping the color word for a punchier English name.
description: An unusual form of tribulation unlike any other (Eps 1105-1142). After absorbing the Luck-Devouring Snakes during his tribulation, Zane enjoys an uncanny streak of good fortune, with anything he wants seeming to fall into his lap; in the source, absorbing more of them was believed to help obtain the World Tree seed.

name: Primordial Chaos Tactic
reason: The source's 'Primal Chaos Secret Technique' was localized as 'Primordial Chaos Tactic', keeping the chaos concept while replacing the wordy 'secret technique' with 'tactic'.
description: Zane's core cultivation method, devised from his master's theory that Primal Chaos Qi is the essence of the universe, setting him on a path completely different from other cultivators (Eps 993-1196). It fundamentally transformed Zane's core, and mastering it required trials most people could not even imagine. Combined with later acquisitions it is expected to 'change everything'.

name: Damian
reason: The source character 'Old Xu' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Damian', dropping the Chinese surname-plus-honorific form.
description: A portly, ragged man who has spent over twenty thousand years on Changsu Island staring at a barren boulder, matching the source's Old Xu who meditated there for 20,000 years alongside Old Chen (localized Landry) (Eps 1069-1111). Half-crazed from the isolation, he is stunned when the silent rock finally reacts after Zane's arrival.

name: Law of Space
reason: Source term 'Law of Space' was kept verbatim, as it already reads naturally in the Western fantasy setting.
description: One of the rarest and most coveted Laws, governing space itself and comprehended in layers (Eps 460-1138). Zane glimpses its first layer early on and his later comprehension of it lets him defeat multiple opponents simultaneously while still in the Spirit-Tribulation Realm, stunning onlookers. Six of the thirty-three textures he later studies carry the Law of Space.

name: Cosmic Age
reason: The source's cosmological cycle term 'Evolution Era' was renamed 'Cosmic Age' to read more naturally as a grand epoch of the universe.
description: The vast cosmological epochs into which the universe's history is divided; every cause and effect is built into the heavens the moment a Cosmic Age is born (Eps 752-1190). The current age is called Cosmos, in which humanity got a head start, and a current Cosmic Age is normally stable. It corresponds to the source's Evolution Era, across hundreds of which certain paths like the Emotion Severing Divine Path were forbidden.

name: Divine Path of Sealed Emotion
reason: The source's 'Emotion Severing Divine Path' was localized as 'Divine Path of Sealed Emotion', softening 'severing' to 'sealed' while keeping the meaning of a godhood path built on suppressing emotion.
description: The Godly Way Zane practices, one of the ultimate paths to power and technically a form of swordsmanship (Eps 1195-1304). In the source it is the Emotion Severing Divine Path, forbidden for hundreds of Evolution Eras, and relying on it alone makes crossing the heavens (the Heavenly Dao) almost unimaginably hard. Powerful figures like the Gilded Warden test how much of it Zane has truly mastered.

name: Hallowed Concord
reason: The source's overtly Buddhist faction, the 'Ten Thousand Buddha Sacred Realm', was renamed 'The Hallowed Concord' to strip the religious specificity while keeping a sacred, collective connotation.
description: One of the great human forces encountered in the late trial arcs (Eps 1219-1306), whose relics include an ancient temple Zane explores. Its people follow a path without the concept of a Godly Way, and lore such as the Strike and the Tome are common knowledge there though almost no one can truly understand them. This matches the source's Ten Thousand Buddha Sacred Realm, the Buddhist power whose path differs completely from the other human factions.

name: Warden
reason: The source's giant golden Buddha guardian of the ancient temple was localized as the 'Gilded Warden', keeping the golden imagery while removing the explicit Buddhist reference.
description: A colossal, lotus-bearing guardian of the temple trial (Eps 1219-1223), apparently corresponding to the source's 30,000-foot golden Buddha that opens its eyes to watch the Inner Yard. It declares that the Dragon-Taming Sentinels (source Subduing Dragon Arhats) cannot be destroyed, and its huge eyes shift from surprise to unmistakable resentment as it scrutinizes Zane, who remains unaware of being watched.

name: Matthew
reason: The character's Chinese name Xie Jun was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Matthew'.
description: Younger brother of Ryder (source Xie Mang), brought along to pick a weapon in the Divine Weapon Hall's dome (Eps 1045-1049). A ninth-stage Life-and-Death Realm cultivator, he is knocked flat by the dome's pressure and angrily admits he completely underestimated it, matching the source's Xie Jun demanding another try. Beside Zane's feat, he is not worth a second glance.

name: Villain World
reason: The source's penal dimension, rendered variously as 'World of Villains' or 'Wicked World/Wicked Realm', was unified as 'Villain World' in the adaptation.
description: A resource-starved penal world to which death-row convicts are banished, with no rules and nothing but survival (Eps 1094-1100). Seven condemned prisoners are brought up from it as the true final test of the Torch Flame trial, with freedom offered to the two who reach the last round. One such prisoner turns out to be the long-lost brother of a trial participant, condemned there with eight hundred years left to his name.

name: Soul Echo
reason: The source's 'Undead Mark' phantom duelists of the tool spirit's final test were renamed 'Soul Echoes', a clearer image of a replayed soul rather than an undead creature.
description: Sword-wielding phantom opponents faced in a trial's final test (Eps 595-600), corresponding to the source's Undead Marks, of which ten must be defeated to pass. The one Zane faces fights with an Emerald Sword and superb defensive technique until Zane breaks its rhythm; beating it gives him a huge confidence boost even though the test is not over.

name: Demon Night War Lords
reason: Combines the show's faction name 'Demon Night' (source Demon Night Clan) with 'War Lord', the localized form of the source rank 'War Elder', to name that clan's elite warriors.
description: Elite warriors of the Demon Night faction at the War Lord rank, appearing throughout the Tower of Sin and Profound Nether Cave arcs (Eps 597-674). They escort their clan's leadership, tense up at displays of overwhelming power, and anxiously keep vigil when a month passes without word from inside the cave. They correspond to the source Demon Night Clan's War Elder-level fighters.

name: Feather Emperor’s Island
reason: Source location 'Feather Emperor Island' was kept nearly verbatim, with a possessive added for natural English ('The Feather Emperor's Island').
description: An island within the Divine Emperor's Secret Land arc (Eps 877-951), battered by hundreds-of-feet-tall tsunamis and crowned at one point by golden swords in the sky. The masters who stayed ashore never learn what Zane found there, and it is where he secretly faces his Lesser Celestial Tribulation. In the source, killing its Ores Devouring Bugs might yield a single soul core.

name: Training Hall
reason: The source's Luo Family 'Martial Arts Hall' was localized as the Lowell 'Training Hall', a plainer English term for the family's combat practice venue.
description: The Lowell family's combat hall where Zane, forced into leather armor and shackles, served as a living training target for two years at the start of the story (Eps 1-15). That he survived the constant beatings convinced onlookers he knew something they didn't. It corresponds to the Luo Family's Martial Arts Hall in the source's opening chapters.

name: Demon
issues: Localized 'Demons' covers several source renderings of the monster races (Yao Clan / Fiend General in the early Sky Forest arc, Demon Clan elsewhere); a deliberate simplification rather than a one-to-one mapping.
reason: The source's monster races (Yao Clan, rendered variously as Fiends or the Demon Clan) were unified under the single familiar term 'Demons' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A hostile non-human race, naturally stronger, tougher, and more enduring than humans (Eps 85-629). They field a military hierarchy of Demon Soldiers, Demon Commanders, and Demon Generals, the latter posing the first significant threat when six of them skewer Zane with bone spurs in the Sky Forest arc. Consorting with Demons during the Purge is treated as treason by the Hall of Judgment.

name: Magic Ward
reason: Yun Luo's unnamed transparent 'barrier' technique in the source was given the proper name 'Magic Ward' for her localized counterpart Yolande Shaw.
description: Yolande Shaw's specialty technique: shimmering, translucent barrier boxes conjured with a flick of the wrist (Eps 129-148). It matches the source's Yun Luo, who summons square, cicada-wing-thin transparent barriers that attacks cannot break. A Magic Ward can hold even a griffin at bay.

name: Leon
reason: The character's Chinese name Ye Chou was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Leon', fitting the cold, methodical arena fighter.
description: A Great Houses fighter serving House Pauling, at rank eight of the Nature Level (Ep 150), matching the source's Ye Chou at Xiantian Realm Level Eight. Despite the massive power gap, he treats the masked, half-step Nature Level Zane as a genuine threat, approaching with eerie deliberation before Zane shatters his concentration and defeats him.

name: Runic Cipher
reason: The source's Eight Trigrams lore (the Qian/Kun/Xun/Zhen/Kan/Li/Gen/Dui formation script) was localized as the 'Runic Cipher', recasting Chinese divination symbols as Western runes.
description: An arcane symbolic script used in ancient formations and mechanisms (Eps 153-979), which only a few characters have studied. It corresponds to the source's Eight Trigrams, whose rotating characters (Kan, Dui, and the rest) guard places like the Jade Dragon Valley pavilion. Knowledge of the Cipher is repeatedly needed to navigate trials and unlock Vitality mechanisms.

name: Spiritual Weapon
issues: Name drift: 9 episodes (Eps 20-211) use the source-flavored 'Spiritual Weapon' where the canonical tier-2 weapon class name is 'Spirit Weapon' (53 episodes).
reason: Same tier-2 weapon class as the canonical 'Spirit Weapon'; 'Spiritual Weapon' is a residual carry-over of the source term 'spiritual weapon' in early episodes.
